about: group-headers: the group cells a frame draws. Each case: each column's label path and width (by index), the order drawn (order[place] is the index; absent, the list's own), the host's pin count (the run in effect is pin.json's rule: the leading columns within half the cells' width), the cells' width, the sideways scroll, and a cell's padding on one side. Expected: the header's group rows (the deepest path) and each cell drawn, level by level, left to right, pinned region first: [level, label, start, end, pinned, left, width, label_x], start..end the whole run's places, left and width the visible part in its region, from the cells area's left, label_x that part's left plus the padding. And the drag half, `gaps`: each column's label path and width, the host's pin count, the cells' width, the sideways scroll, a dragged block of places [first, last], and the pointer's x (the cells area's pixels) → whether the block lifts, and the gap (or null), its `to`, and its side, by reorder.json's gap rule over the block's parent's children (a gap among them, by their centers, inside the parent's span).

controls.groups-by-place: DataTable's spans: the runs found over the paths in index order and laid on the places, so a move leaves the groups where they were.
controls.no-split-at-edge: A run across pin's edge drawn whole in the region where it starts, the scrolled region drawing none of it.
controls.label-centered: The label at the run's middle, not at its visible part's left: a wide group scrolled half out loses it.
controls.gap-outside-parent: A drag's gaps found among every column over the whole table, as without groups: a column leaves its group, a group lands inside another.
controls.gap-by-column-centers: The gap after the child holding the last column whose center, not the child's, is left of the pointer: past a sibling group's first column is past the group.

cases.name: two-levels-at-rest
cases.why: Neighbors agreeing through a level share its cell; a path shorter than a level leaves a blank there; no path, no cell.

cases.name: blanks-under-a-shorter-path
cases.why: Three levels: each column's name stays on the bottom row, a shorter path's levels below its last group blank.

cases.name: scrolled-half-out
cases.why: A wide group scrolled half out of view is cut at the view's left, its label kept at the visible part's left; one cut at the view's right ends there.

cases.name: split-at-the-edge
cases.why: A run across pin's edge draws a cell in each region, each labeled, both with the whole run's places; the scrolled half is cut at the edge.

cases.name: the-cap-splits
cases.why: The host pins 4, but only 2 fit in half the view: the cap in effect falls inside the group, which is drawn split there.

cases.name: a-move-splits-a-run
cases.why: A path travels with its column: a column moved into another group's columns splits that group into two runs, a cell each, both labeled.

cases.name: no-groups
cases.why: No path: no group row, the header as without the feature.

gaps.name: a-column-within-its-group
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. Column 0, in x, past column 1's center (150): the gap after it, x's end.

gaps.name: held-at-its-groups-edge
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. Column 0 with the pointer over B: x's last gap, never outside x.

gaps.name: a-group-among-its-siblings
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. x among A's children (x, y, column 4), past y's center (300): the gap after y.

gaps.name: past-a-siblings-first-column
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. x with the pointer past y's first column's center (250) but not y's (300): the gap beside x, none.

gaps.name: a-group-held-in-its-parent
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. x with the pointer over B: A's last gap, past column 4.

gaps.name: a-top-group-among-the-tables-children
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. B among the table's children (A, B, column 7), left of A's center (250): the first gap.

gaps.name: a-block-cutting-a-group
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. Columns 1-2 cut x: the block doesn't lift.

gaps.name: right-of-its-parent-its-last-gap
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. The view 300 wide scrolled to 500, so only B and the last column show: column 2, in y, with y wholly left of the view, takes y's last gap.

gaps.name: a-split-group-lands-whole
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. The host pins 3, splitting A at its fourth column: A dragged right of the last column lands wholly scrolled, the count 0.

gaps.name: a-group-pinned-before-a-split-one
gaps.why: Eight columns: A over 0-4, its x over 0-1 and y over 2-3, B over 5-6, the last in none. The host pins 3: B dragged into the run, left of A's pinned part's center (150), lands pinned, wholly, before A.

gaps.name: a-group-pinned-across-the-edge
gaps.why: A, B, C, two columns each; the host pins A. B dragged left of A's center (100) lands pinned.

gaps.name: a-pinned-group-unpinned-where-it-is
gaps.why: A, B, C, two columns each; the host pins A. A dragged just right of the edge (200), left of B's center: the run's end, across it, unpins A where it is.

gaps.name: every-column-pinned-pointer-past-them
gaps.why: A, B, C, two columns each, all six pinned (600 px within half the view): with the pointer right of the edge, no scrolled column shows, and the table's own span gives no gap there, as reorder.json's rule has it.

gaps.name: a-split-sibling-from-its-scrolled-half
gaps.why: A over 0-2 and three columns in none; the host pins 2, splitting A. Column 4 with the pointer right of the edge, left of A's scrolled half's center (250): A's start is in the pinned region, so in the scrolled one A's gap is its end, where the line is drawn.

gaps.name: a-split-sibling-from-its-pinned-half
gaps.why: A over 0-2 and three columns in none; the host pins 2, splitting A. Column 4 with the pointer left of the edge, right of A's pinned half's center (100): A's end is in the scrolled region, so in the pinned one A's gap is its start, and the column lands pinned there.
